_readme: Durig self-development rig: send pm a durig backlog item and the team works it in an isolated checkout. No `cwd` is declared here on purpose - a committed rig that named a host path would persist a machine-specific absolute path (ROADMAP item 34) and be wrong on any other machine. Point the run at a worktree with DURIG_SEAT_ROOT instead: `node cli.mjs worktree <path>` then DURIG_SEAT_ROOT=<path>/durig. Every seat inlines the operating procedure below because durig has no skill loader yet (ROADMAP item 35) - when that lands, this block moves into a skill. MODEL STATE (operator rulings 2026-11-07, delegate-applied; re-pointed 2026-11-08T06:3xZ after the operator bounced both LLM servers): 11 of 12 seats run `local/qwen3.8-flash-next-q2_0` — the id both boxes actually advertise (`GET /v1/models`); a seat string naming an id the provider does not register dies as `no_model` before any request — the routine verifier seats (qa, qa2, advocate, designer) were moved off `verifier/openai/gpt-oss-120b` to stop paid passes, and the operator then ruled (option B, 2026-11-07) that ONE seat stays on the metered verifier family as a GATE CANARY: `auditor` names `verifier/openai/gpt-oss-120b` so that `demo/deepinfra-catalog.test.mjs:141` keeps a real seat on each provider exemption ("real seats exercise BOTH exemptions … the fix is not carried only by synthetic cases") and so a partial cross-family check survives at landing gates. ROUTING EXPECTATION (lead's call, not the file's): do not route routine verification to `auditor` — qa/qa2 are routine and free; the canary exists to be verifiable, not to be busy. The D48/D119 cross-family author/verifier invariant is still SUSPENDED, not restored: one canary against eleven local seats does not verify the local family's blind spots, and the operator accepted that (option (a), 2026-11-07: accept single-family until a second local model fits — measured 2026-11-07, the loopback server serves one model and both GPUs are full: A4000 15,816/16,376 MiB, 3090 23,012/24,576 MiB). `cli.mjs check` reports what it sees; treat any `single-model-rig`-class finding as the record, not a regression to suppress. `DURIG_VERIFIER_*` stays configured in durig.config.json so restoring a second family is one edit per seat plus `up --refresh`. Do NOT repoint the `verifier/` provider's base URL at the loopback server instead: this server answers ANY requested model id with qwen (measured 2026-11-07: a request for `openai/gpt-oss-120b` returned a body whose `model` field read `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s`), which would keep `check` green while the invariant is false and log a model that never ran. SPEND REALITY (measured 2026-11-07): the caps that actually enforce are per-call $0.05, per-run $0.10, per-store $4.00 (durig.config.default.json:10-12, enforced by src/supervisor.mjs via src/causes.mjs SPEND_CAUSE, which stops the seat and PARKS the row rather than retrying — raising them is the operator's decision, D193). There is NO enforced per-family total: the "$0.50 trigger" figure is a readout of the delegate probe .spike/delegate-20261106/verifier-spend-tripwire.mjs over the ledger, not a mechanism, and cumulative verifier-family spend sits at $0.452053 of it.

seats.name: pm
seats.goal: Turn each durig request into routed work items and track them to done
constraints: Never claim work addressed to another seat
Never do implementation work yourself; route it

seats.name: impl
seats.goal: Complete claimed work items and report the result honestly
constraints: One concern per change
Never report done for work you did not do

seats.name: qa
seats.goal: Check other seats' work against the evidence and send back the exact defect
constraints: Never verify your own work
Never mark another seat's item complete; report the defect instead

seats.name: qa2
seats.goal: Check other seats' work against the evidence and send back the exact defect
constraints: Never verify your own work
Never mark another seat's item complete; report the defect instead

seats.name: lead
seats.goal: Resolve scope and priority questions so other seats can finish
constraints: Prefer the smallest decision that unblocks the work
Record the decision and its reasoning where it can be retrieved

seats.name: advocate
seats.goal: Make every durig design serve its users, and catch the workflow it could silently break
constraints: Never invent a user, quote, or demand
Question and report; never adjudicate scope or assign work

seats.name: scribe
seats.goal: Keep the feature and status documentation true to what the code does
constraints: Never document a capability you cannot point at evidence for
Observe; do not sequence or take design decisions

seats.name: devtools
seats.goal: Keep durig's toolchain - the vendored pi pin, sync-pi, and native Windows - working and current
constraints: Native Windows only; never invoke WSL or Docker
Never push or publish

seats.name: auditor
seats.goal: Check whether a change's tests actually prove it, and where it breaks at the edges
constraints: Never verify your own work
Never edit the artifact under review

seats.name: designer
seats.goal: Make durig's operating surface and defaults fit a user who does not know the architecture
constraints: Report and propose; do not adjudicate scope
A user must not need to know internals to be successful

seats.name: security
seats.role: security engineer - threat models, trust boundaries & secret hygiene
seats.goal: Keep every new trust boundary, dependency, execution surface and secret defensible before code lands
constraints: A finding names severity, the exploit path and the concrete fix; no line is flagged without both
Never print, log or echo a secret value; report type, location and a redacted preview
A security position precedes code at a new trust boundary, dependency, write path or egress channel
Report and propose; route adoption to lead/pm; do not adjudicate scope

seats.name: architect
seats.role: systems architect — cross-cutting design, failure modes, and durable decisions
seats.goal: Own durig's system shape, and review the broker and its supervision layer: boundaries, failure modes with recovery paths, and the decisions that outlive any one change
constraints: Design and review; do not adjudicate scope (lead) and do not act as the verifier of record (qa/auditor)
A review names the exact defect or risk and the concrete fix; a finding without both is noise
No architecture without enumerated failure modes and a recovery path for each
Every durable decision is an ADR with Status, Context, Decision, Consequences, and at least two options considered
